Given the extremely brief flash-fiction format of the story, the single present character, Clara, is developed at an appropriate level of complexity. Through subtle body language (refusing to let go of her travel bag, absentmindedly tasting the water) and her sensory observations of the house—specifically noting that the house no longer smells of her deceased mother, but rather the "absence of everything"—the reader gets a believable sense of her grief, hesitation, and history with the place. She feels like a real person experiencing a quiet, eerie moment rather than a flat device used merely to deliver the final twist.
